description: Three-panel composite of instrumented Charpy impact load-deflection data for two low-alloy ultrahigh-strength steels. (a) Load/KN (0-50, left axis) versus Deflection/mm (0-10, bottom axis) for both steels; the legend identifies the blue curve as 0Al and the purple curve as 1.3Al, a square marker as P_GY and a circle marker as P_M. The blue 0Al curve peaks near the 40 KN gridline at ~2.1 mm, the purple 1.3Al curve peaks just below 40 KN at ~2.6 mm; the square P_GY markers lie on the rising flank below 30 KN. After the peak both traces drop steeply and oscillate around zero load to 10 mm with no crack-arrest plateau. (b) 0Al steel: the load trace is repeated with a right-hand Energy/J axis (0-140); the integrated area is shaded yellow for E_i = 45.0 J and purple for E_p = 17.4 J, a dashed line marks P_m = 39.7 KN, and a rising red cumulative-energy curve plateaus at KU₂ = 62.4 J. (c) 1.3Al steel: identical layout giving P_m = 38.6 KN, E_i = 62.0 J, E_p = 21.0 J, KU₂ = 83.0 J. The figure demonstrates that despite near-equal peak loads, the Al-containing steel absorbs markedly more crack-initiation and propagation energy.

subfigures.description: Load/KN versus Deflection/mm curves for both steels: blue 0Al curve and purple 1.3Al curve, legend plus square (P_GY) and circle (P_M) symbols. 0Al peaks slightly below 40 KN at ~2.1 mm and drops sharply by ~2.5 mm; 1.3Al peaks at ~39 KN at ~2.6 mm, dropping at ~3 mm; both then oscillate near zero to 10 mm.

0Al steel load-deflection trace with dual axes (Load/KN left 0-45, Energy/J right 0-140). Printed values: P_m = 39.7 KN, E_i = 45.0 J (yellow shaded area), E_p = 17.4 J (purple shaded area), KU₂ = 62.4 J red dashed plateau.
1.3Al steel load-deflection trace with dual axes, same layout as (b). Printed values: P_m = 38.6 KN, E_i = 62.0 J (yellow area), E_p = 21.0 J (purple area), KU₂ = 83.0 J red dashed plateau.

observations.observation: In panel (a) the legend labels the blue curve 0Al and the purple curve 1.3Al; the square symbol denotes P_GY and the open circle denotes P_M.
In panel (a) the 0Al (blue) curve reaches its maximum at about the 40 KN gridline at ~2.1 mm deflection, while the 1.3Al (purple) curve peaks slightly lower, at ~2.6 mm deflection.
The square P_GY markers in panel (a) lie on the ascending branch of both curves below the 30 KN gridline, i.e. well before the maximum load.
After the peak, both curves in (a) fall steeply and oscillate close to zero load out to 10 mm, showing no sustained crack-arrest plateau.
Panel (b) prints P_m = 39.7 KN, E_i = 45.0 J, E_p = 17.4 J and KU₂ = 62.4 J for the 0Al steel.
Panel (c) prints P_m = 38.6 KN, E_i = 62.0 J, E_p = 21.0 J and KU₂ = 83.0 J for the 1.3Al steel.

In panels (b) and (c) the crack-initiation energy is shaded yellow and the crack-propagation energy purple, and the two shaded areas sum exactly to the KU₂ plateau of the red cumulative-energy curve (45.0 + 17.4 = 62.4 J; 62.0 + 21.0 = 83.0 J).
The caption states that (a) compares the two steels while (b) and (c) show the 0Al and 1.3Al steels respectively.

The citing text states that the 0Al and 1.3Al steels reached their peak loads (P_M) at deflections of 2.06 mm and 2.55 mm respectively, followed by rapid load drops; these numbers are not printed in the image.
The citing text states that crack propagation accelerated at ~2.5 mm for the 0Al steel and ~3 mm for the 1.3Al steel.
The citing text states E_i and E_p were 45.0 J and 17.4 J for the 0Al steel and 62.0 J and 21.0 J for the 1.3Al steel, matching the values printed in panels (b) and (c).
The citing text states that compared with the 0Al steel the 1.3Al steel showed a 37.8 % higher E_i and a 20.7 % higher E_p, and that its E_p exceeds the 0Al counterpart by 4.6 J.
The citing text defines P_M as the load at which crack initiation occurs, with E_i representing crack-initiation resistance and E_p crack-propagation resistance.

unreadable_items: Panel (a): the peak loads are marked only by symbols (P_M circles) and are not printed as numbers, so the peak values were read from their position relative to the 40 KN gridline, not from a printed label.
